The South African jurist Navi Pillay, the Nobel Peace Prize recipient, is one
of the most distinguished human rights lawyers and judges of the past few
decades. Early in her extraordinary career, she embodied the struggle against
apartheid in South Africa, where she defended anti-apartheid activists. As a
judge in the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and in the
International Criminal Court (ICC), she embodied the development of
international criminal law, helping to advance accountability for crimes and
shape the human rights system. As UN high commissioner for human rights, and
later as chair of the UN Commission of Inquiry on Palestine, she documented
violations, supported mechanisms for protecting rights, and scrutinised
states' responsibility for violations - culminating in the commission's 2025
finding that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

By granting Pillay the prize, the Nobel committee has infuriated Israel, which
had [called for the commission to be
abolished](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8641wv0n4go) following its
finding of genocide, and it has rebuffed President Donald Trump, who had made
[no secret of his desire to win the
prize](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/trump-says-he-deserves-nobel-
peace-prize-has-doubts-he-will-get-it-2026-10-07/).
